rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elicit all 10 compounds while minimizing risk of truncation. This should reveal the overall elution window and whether early peaks are unretained or late peaks still require stronger/faster conditions.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to reduce t_last below 10 min without letting the closest pair collapse. A modestly steeper gradient plus a small temperature increase should shorten the run substantially while preserving the currently strong minimum resolution.

The steepening and temperature increase drove the critical pair (6,7) into near co-elution, so back off one slope step while keeping the higher temperature that nearly achieved the 10 min target. This should restore that pair’s resolution while keeping t_last close to 10 min.

The critical pair is strongly temperature-sensitive and remained under-resolved at 45 C even after lengthening tG, so test whether dropping back to the original slope while keeping 45 C restores resolution enough to beat injection 2. This isolates temperature versus slope effects on the problematic pair.

The data show the critical pair loses resolution mainly as temperature rises, so move below 40 C to improve selectivity while keeping the well-behaved broad gradient constant. This will map the temperature dependence of the limiting pair and indicate whether a cooler run can maintain full resolution before we optimize speed again.

All peaks elute within a relatively narrow effective solvent range, so trim the high-organic end and keep the gradient focused on the observed window while returning to 40 C where all pairs were fully resolved. This should preserve selectivity and may shorten the last peak enough to improve on the current best without the severe compression seen at 45 C.

At 40 C the narrowed window still gave comfortable full resolution, so the next move is to shorten the gradient aggressively and see how much time can be cut before the critical mid-cluster collapses. This directly probes the speed limit at the more favorable temperature/selectivity setting.

The last peak is already under 10 min, so the remaining improvement is to recover full resolution credit for the 6/7 pair without giving back too much speed. Narrowing the gradient window slightly should reduce local gradient steepness around the mid-eluting cluster and may lift that pair above 1.5 while keeping t_last near 10 min.

The 6/7 pair is now essentially at the 1.5 threshold, so lengthen the gradient by one step while keeping the promising narrowed window and temperature fixed. This should push that pair to full credit, and if t_last stays under about 10.25 min it can surpass the current best.

The narrowed window improved the critical pair, so take one more small step narrower at the same fast gradient to try to push 6/7 cleanly above 1.5 without the large time penalty seen when tG was lengthened. The late peak should move somewhat later, but there is still room to beat the current score if resolution reaches full credit with only a modest t_last increase.

At 40 C the 0.75 window is nearly optimal but still just misses full credit on the critical pair, while 35 C changed the identity of the closest pair and generally expanded the mid-cluster. Testing the same narrowed fast gradient at 35 C checks whether cooler conditions recover full resolution with a smaller time penalty than the broader 20 min run.

The first peak is still comfortably retained, so raising phi0 by one step may trim overall retention and pull the last peak under 10 min while minimally affecting the already near-threshold critical pair. This tests whether a shifted but equally wide window can improve time enough to beat the current best.

You have achieved the maximum CRF, so the only sensible exploitation step is to see whether the gradient can be shortened further while keeping all adjacent pairs at or above 1.5 and t_last under 10 min. This probes whether the current optimum has any remaining slack in run time.

Since 10 min was too steep, explore whether a slightly narrower window than the optimum can preserve full resolution while reducing the already sub-10-minute last peak further. This is a local robustness check around the maximum-CRF method without repeating it.

Check the opposite side of the local optimum by widening the upper end one step from the best method while keeping phi0 and tG fixed. If the critical pair is sensitive to local slope around its elution range, this will confirm whether 0.75 is truly the best phi1 setting or whether a slightly broader window can retain full credit with acceptable timing.

The first peak is still fairly early with the best method, so raise phi0 one more step to see if the last peak can be shortened further while keeping the mid-cluster selectivity acceptable. This is the most plausible remaining one-step time optimization around the current optimum.

Two methods now give CRF 1.000, and the higher phi0 version shortens the run slightly; the next logical test is one more step higher in phi0 to see whether additional time can be shaved without driving the first peak into the near-void region or hurting the critical pair. This explores the remaining headroom on the low-organic end.

Having mapped phi0 at 40 C, test whether a modest temperature increase at the stronger phi0 setting preserves full resolution while further shortening the run. This checks for a second 1.000-CRF plateau with a faster method near the current optimum.

Since 0.15/0.75/12/40 also achieved CRF 1.000, test whether there is extra resolution margin at this higher phi0 setting that could support a slightly longer but more robust method around the same selectivity. This helps confirm whether the 1.000 region is broad or knife-edge near the current operating point.

Map the upper-edge robustness of the second 1.000-CRF optimum by widening phi1 one step at the same phi0, tG, and T. If the critical pair remains above 1.5 while t_last stays under 10 min, this would identify a broader operating window around the maximum.

Complete the local map around the second optimum by testing one step lower phi1. This checks whether the best 1.000 condition at phi0 0.15 sits on a plateau or whether 0.75 is the unique upper-window setting that keeps the critical pair and the last peak both just inside the optimum limits.

With two 1.000 methods already found, use remaining injections to confirm robustness boundaries in temperature at the original optimum composition. This directly tests whether the perfect method is specific to 40 C or whether some hotter setting can maintain full credit while preserving the sub-10 min last peak.

The remaining unknown boundary around the optimum is cooler temperature, and 35 C with lower phi0 changed the critical pair identity dramatically. Testing 30 C at the best composition will complete the temperature map and confirm whether 40 C is indeed the unique selectivity sweet spot.

With the temperature map complete and two perfect methods identified, use one of the last injections to test whether the higher-phi0 optimum has enough extra margin to tolerate a shorter gradient than the original optimum. This is the most plausible remaining route to a faster perfect method without changing the favorable 40 C selectivity.

For the final run, probe one last nearby composition around the optimum by widening phi1 above 0.80 while keeping the successful phi0, tG, and temperature fixed. This tests whether the 1.000 region extends to a broader upper window, although the current best methods at 0.10/0.75/12/40 and 0.15/0.75/12/40 remain the top performers.
